current.text: The projected starting five is Cade Cunningham, Duncan Robinson, Ausar Thompson, John Collins and Jalen Duren, the same as last season.
Jalen Duren's contract situation was still unresolved in the 2026-09-30 note. A trade would bring back another center, and a holdout was a worry.
The newest preview (2026-10-03) treats Duren as back and projects him as the starting center.
One expert does not expect Detroit to start the season with Paul Reed at center.
Isaiah Stewart is gone. Paul Reed is now the main backup center, so there is less frontcourt depth behind Duren.
As Duren's backup, Reed would play about 20 minutes a night.
Because Duren's situation is unresolved, Paul Reed is worth a late flyer.
Ugonna Onyenso, a rookie on a two-way contract, is the other center on the roster.
Power forward depth is very weak unless Ausar Thompson and Ron Holland play the four.
The projected bench order is Isaiah Joe as sixth man, then Ron Holland, Paul Reed and Daniss Jenkins. Prince or Kevin Huerter gets the last rotation spot.
Last season the team used a deep 12 to 13 player rotation that limited everyone's minutes.
The team lost creation with Tobias Harris gone. It has very few creators besides Cade Cunningham.
The lack of other creators could push Cunningham's assists up, unless Daniss Jenkins takes a bigger ball-handling role.
With Duren back, the team will still have some spacing issues.
If the plan to use Ausar Thompson and Duren on the ball is failing by January, Detroit may trade for a secondary playmaker at the deadline.
Coop projects 50 to 51 wins and a third or fourth seed in the East. The betting win total is 49.5, sixth in the league. Tanking is not a concern.
Our fantasy playoff schedule is 4-3-4, so 11 games in weeks 19 to 21, fourth most in the league.
The team has 15 back-to-backs, about average. No rest risks are expected.
The team has no notable injuries.

durable.text: The team is built on defense. The front office wants only enough offense, not an offensive superstar.
One expert says coach J.B. Bickerstaff has repeatedly misled about Ausar Thompson's minutes and health.
Treat Bickerstaff's updates on minutes and injuries with caution.

tags.detail: Projected for 50 to 51 wins and a third or fourth seed. Win total 49.5, rank 6.
tags.new_meaning: Projected to win clearly more than half its games, so tanking and late-season shutdowns are unlikely.

tags.detail: Front office wants only enough offense. Creation and spacing are thin beyond Cunningham.
tags.new_meaning: The team is built around defense, with limited offensive creation and spacing.

note: Detroit is a winning, defense-first team with a strong 4-3-4 playoff schedule and no expected rest risk. Cade Cunningham gains as the only real creator, and Paul Reed is a cheap late flyer while Duren's contract situation stays unclear. Watch early whether Duren is fully back, how tightly Bickerstaff trims last season's 12 to 13 player rotation, and whether Daniss Jenkins takes ball-handling work.
